questiontext.text: In an n-gram model, the next token is predicted from what?

answer.text: The previous n-1 tokens (the context)

feedback.text: Correct — the preceding n-1 tokens form the context.

answer.text: The entire document from the start

feedback.text: No — an n-gram only looks back n-1 tokens.

answer.text: A single fixed token, ignoring history

feedback.text: No — the context is the previous n-1 tokens, not one.

answer.text: The token that comes after it

feedback.text: No — prediction uses preceding tokens, not future ones.

generalfeedback.text: An n-gram model conditions on the previous n-1 tokens, called the context.

questiontext.text: What data structure stores the mapping from context to next-token counts?

answer.text: A hash map keyed by the context

feedback.text: Yes — a hash map maps each context to its next-token counts.

answer.text: A sorted array of all tokens

feedback.text: No — that does not directly map contexts to distributions.

answer.text: A single global counter

feedback.text: No — counts are per-context, not one global number.

generalfeedback.text: A hash map stores context to next-token counts for O(1) average lookup.

questiontext.text: Given a context's counts, how is the next token chosen?

answer.text: It is sampled from the distribution, e.g. proportional to counts

feedback.text: Yes — sampling (optionally with temperature) draws from the distribution.

answer.text: Always take the alphabetically first candidate

feedback.text: No — that ignores the learned distribution.

answer.text: Pick a token uniformly at random ignoring counts

feedback.text: No — sampling is weighted by the counts.

generalfeedback.text: The next token is sampled from the context's distribution, e.g. proportional to counts, optionally with temperature.

questiontext.text: What is the trade-off of using a larger n?

answer.text: It captures more context but the counts become sparser

feedback.text: Yes — longer contexts are seen less often, so estimates get sparse.

answer.text: It captures less context and uses more memory for no benefit

feedback.text: No — larger n captures more, not less, context.

answer.text: It removes the need to store any counts

feedback.text: No — counts are still required regardless of n.

generalfeedback.text: A higher n captures more context but is sparser, since long contexts recur rarely.

questiontext.text: Which statements about the n-gram next-token model are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: The context is the previous n-1 tokens

feedback.text: Yes — that preceding window is the context.

answer.text: The next token is sampled from the context's count distribution

feedback.text: Yes — sampling is proportional to counts, optionally temperature-scaled.

answer.text: A larger n always makes the counts denser

feedback.text: No — larger n makes the counts sparser.

answer.text: It must scan the whole corpus for every prediction

feedback.text: No — a hash map gives fast lookup of the context.

generalfeedback.text: The model conditions on the previous n-1 tokens, samples from hashed counts, and grows sparser as n increases.

questiontext.text: The next token can be sampled from the distribution rather than always taking the single most frequent one.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — sampling (optionally with temperature) introduces variety.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Sampling from the distribution is exactly how the next token is drawn.

questiontext.text: Increasing n makes the observed context counts denser and less sparse.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — larger n captures more context but is sparser.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — a higher n is sparser because long contexts recur rarely.

answer.text: context

feedback.text: Correct.

feedback.text: Correct.
